slot.brief: Given a di- or trisubstituted carbonyl compound (figure with structure), ask for all correct tests/reactions it will show — codes like (i) Tollens positive, (ii) Cannizzaro positive, (iii) iodoform positive, etc.

stem:
Consider the compound shown in the figure. Which of the following statements are correct?
(i) It gives a positive Tollens test.
(ii) It undergoes Cannizzaro reaction.
(iii) It gives a positive iodoform test.
(iv) It forms an oxime with hydroxylamine.

verdicts.working: The structure is CH₃COCHO (methylglyoxal). Its aldehyde group gives Tollens’ test and, having no α-hydrogen, undergoes Cannizzaro reaction. The CH₃CO– group gives the iodoform test, and its carbonyl groups form oximes with hydroxylamine. Thus all four statements are correct.

working:
(i) Tollens: aldehyde reduces Ag⁺ → positive. (ii) Cannizzaro: aldehyde has no α‑H (adjacent C is carbonyl, no H) → positive. (iii) Iodoform: CH₃CO– (methyl ketone) → positive. (iv) Oxime: both carbonyls react with NH₂OH → positive. Hence all four are correct.

Independent check: The structure is CH₃COCHO (methylglyoxal). Its aldehyde group gives Tollens’ test and, having no α-hydrogen, undergoes Cannizzaro reaction. The CH₃CO– group gives the iodoform test, and its carbonyl groups form oximes with hydroxylamine. Thus all four statements are correct.
solution:
For methylglyoxal, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCHO$, the aldehyde group gives Tollens’ test and, with no $alpha$-hydrogen, undergoes Cannizzaro reaction.
The $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group gives the iodoform test, and both carbonyl groups react with $\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$ to form oximes.
Hence all four statements are correct.

figure.description: Skeletal structure of pyruvaldehyde: CH3–C(=O)–CHO. The molecule has a methyl group bonded to a carbonyl carbon (C=O), which in turn is bonded to an aldehyde group (CHO). No hydrogen atoms are shown on carbon atoms bonded to oxygen.

draft.working: (i) Tollens: aldehyde reduces Ag⁺ → positive. (ii) Cannizzaro: aldehyde has no α‑H (adjacent C is carbonyl, no H) → positive. (iii) Iodoform: CH₃CO– (methyl ketone) → positive. (iv) Oxime: both carbonyls react with NH₂OH → positive. Hence all four are correct.
draft.distractor_notes: Options (A) and (C) miss key tests; (B) incorrectly omits Cannizzaro because some students may think the aldehyde has an α‑hydrogen due to the adjacent methyl group, not realizing the α‑carbon is the carbonyl C with no H.
